title: SIEM & Evidence Automation: Incident Response Runbook
content:
Purpose:
This runbook captures on-call procedures and post-incident workflows for incidents that require rapid evidence collection, SIEM exports, or RBAC-related investigation. It focuses on automating evidence snapshots, ensuring audit-log fidelity (schema-specific), and producing a defensible postmortem. This doc is intended for the security on-call, SOC analysts, SRE on-call, and engineering owners.

Scope: 
- Incidents involving suspicious access patterns (credential compromise, privilege escalation attempts)
- Automated or manual evidence exports to SIEMs (Splunk/Elastic/Datadog)
- Cases where RBAC v2 policy changes or failures may be involved
- Preservation of logs/evidence for legal/regulatory follow-up

Quick links (operational):
- Audit log schema spec: drive:shared_drives/security-and-compliance/audit-log-schema-v2.md (canonical)
- RBAC v2 policy reference: internal/rbac-v2/README (confluence id CONFLUENCE-RBAC-V2)
- Evidence automation repo: github.com/redwood-inference/sec-evidence-automation
- SIEM connectors: runbook library -> siem-connectors.md

On-call responsibilities (first 30 minutes):
1) Triage & scope: acknowledge alert in #sec-oncall within 2 minutes. Post short summary: "acknowledged, triaging" and assign severity.
2) Identify affected principals and assets: run quick probes against our audit log service and RBAC audit endpoint. Use the helper script: tools/snap-audit.sh --since=1h --filter="principal:<id>". If script fails, fallback to manual query in audit UI.
3) Preserve evidence snapshot (automated): execute evidence snapshot job (k8s job: sec-evidence-snapshot) which does:
   - Export of audit logs (jsonl) for the time window to the secure evidence bucket (s3://redwood-sec-evidence/YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS)
   - Hashing (sha256) of each file and manifest creation
   - Capture of RBAC policy at time of incident (rbac-policies/current.json) and any recent changes from the policy-change feed
   - Export of relevant system logs (gateway, auth service, token-issuer)
Note: if automation is failing, create a manual evidence bundle and record SHA256 sums locally and in the incident ticket.
4) SIEM export (if needed): kick an export job to the configured SIEM destination. For Splunk/ELK/Datadog we maintain a single-click export in our internal portal: /sec/exports -> select evidence bundle -> export->select destination. For emergency exports, run: tools/siem-export --bundle s3://path --dest splunk:hec://... --fields=fields-map-v2.json

Investigation playbooks (choose the one that matches):
A) Suspected credential compromise / API key abuse
   - Indicators: unusual geolocation, high request rate, API key used from new service, token reuse across many principals
   - Actions: rotate API key / invalidate session tokens for the affected principal (auth service: POST /admin/sessions/invalidate principal=<id>). If a service account: rotate and redeploy secrets via secret-manager automation.
   - Evidence: pull audit records for token issuance and token use. Preserve full header set (user-agent, ip, x-forwarded-for). Export to SIEM for correlation.
   - RBAC check: snapshot the principal's roles and recent role changes. Look for recently added high-privilege roles. Query: rbac-audit --principal <id> --since 72h.

B) Privilege escalation attempt / unauthorized RBAC change
   - Indicators: API calls to /rbac/roles or unexpected policy update entries in audit log schema (field: event_type=rbac_change, change_type=grant/modify).
   - Actions: freeze policy-change pipeline (if using automated policy CI: flip feature flag sec.rbac.change.accept=false), revoke the change author’s elevated tokens, and create a forensics snapshot of the policy repo at HEAD and pre-HEAD.
   - Evidence automation: include commit hashes and signed approval emails in bundle. If the change was pushed via gitops, capture repo webhook payloads and CI logs.

C) Data exfiltration suspicion (large volume read/exports)
   - Indicators: spikes in read/embeddings requests, large downloads from storage buckets, or unusual exports triggered.
   - Actions: throttle or block the involved routes (rate-limit keys, apply temporary firewall rules). Work with storage team to snapshot bucket objects and enable object-level logging.
   - SIEM: create a correlation search for read-volume anomalies and attach the evidence snapshot.

Preserving chain-of-custody (must do every time):
- Always use the automated evidence snapshot job when available. If manual, note the operator, timestamp, exact commands used, and compute and record SHA256 on the incident ticket.
- Upload artifacts to the secure evidence bucket and set ACL to readonly for sec-oncall + legal.
- Add the evidence S3 path to the incident ticket with the hash manifest.

Audit log schema & field mapping (operational notes):
- We rely on audit-log-schema-v2. Key fields to include for forensic quality:
   - timestamp (ISO8601), event_id (uuid), principal_id, principal_type (user, service), event_type, resource_type, resource_id, action, ip_address, user_agent, request_id, request_headers (subset), response_status, bytes_transferred, metadata (freeform)
- For SIEM exports always map into the canonical fields map: fields-map-v2.json. SIEM autotags must include incident_id and evidence_bundle_id.

Automation healthchecks (pre-incident quick checklist):
- Confirm sec-evidence-snapshot k8s job succeeded in last 24h.
- Confirm SIEM connector heartbeat is green (last success < 5m).
- Confirm audit-log ingest lag < 60s.
- Confirm RBAC policy-change feed consumer is not in error state.
If any check fails, raise P1 to infra and notify #sec-ops.

Communication playbook:
- Initial: #sec-oncall ack + short summary, tag incident, set severity and assign primary and secondary.
- Exec brief (for P1/P0): product security lead + head of SRE to be notified via @exec-alerts and a short written blurb: scope, impact, mitigation, next steps.
- Customer or legal escalation: route through customer-success and legal. Do not share raw evidence; provide summary only unless legal requests exports.

Post-incident: security postmortem template (fill and publish into Confluence):
- Title
- Incident ID
- Date/Time window
- Severity
- Summary (2–3 sentences)
- Timeline (minute-level for detection/containment actions)
- Detection: which alert or user report triggered triage
- Root cause analysis (technical + process failures)
- Evidence collected (S3 paths, SIEM export ids, hashes)
- Remediation taken (short-term and long-term)
- Impacted customers/systems and disclosure notes
- Action items (owner, due date, status)
- Lessons learned and recommended policy changes (e.g., RBAC hardening, audit retention increase, SIEM correlation rules)

Retention and legal hold notes: 
- Evidence used for legal/regulatory cases: apply legal-hold label and extend retention per legal instructions. Contact legal@redwood-inference for hold procedures.
- Default evidence retention: 90 days in secure evidence bucket; extended holds override.

Appendix: useful commands & examples
- Snapshot only audit logs for a principal: tools/snap-audit.sh --principal="alice@redwood.com" --since=24h --out=./alice-24h.jsonl
- Trigger SIEM export: tools/siem-export --bundle s3://redwood-sec-evidence/20250110-103000 --dest splunk --map=fields-map-v2.json
- Invalidate sessions for a principal: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://auth.internal/admin/sessions/invalidate -d '{"principal":"<id>"}'

Open questions / TODOs (working items):
- Add automated legal-hold tagging at upload time for evidence bundles (tracking JIRA-SIEM-EXPORT-89).
- Improve mapping for embeddings/large-vector requests to capture request payload hash (privacy constraints exist).
- Add more SIEM playbook templates for Elastic and Datadog (currently Splunk-first).

Owner notes: This is an evolving operational doc. If you use it in a live incident, please paste the incident ticket ID back here and add any command snippets you ran to the bottom of this doc so the next on-call benefits.

End of runbook.
